conventions.convention: PSUs partition the finite element population into nonempty sets. SSU values and PSU totals are fixed under design probability; one-stage sampling completely enumerates selected PSUs.

Given the selected PSU set, secondary samples are independent with fixed PSU-specific laws. Expansion estimators require positive first-order inclusion probabilities at both stages; pair-inclusion probabilities may be zero.
The SRSWOR variance theorem assumes M ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ m ≤ M, and defines S_T² using denominator M−1.

The equal-size design effect is a no-FPC superpopulation comparison: k independent identically distributed PSU vectors of size m_c ≥ 2, common marginal variance σ² > 0 and common within-PSU covariance ρσ², compared with km_c independent marginal draws.
The general two-stage variance theorem assumes AC through its published conditional-expectation and conditional-variance suppliers; the finite enumerated example does not use that branch.

The unequal-size counterexample defines DEFF as a ratio of model-averaged conditional design variances, using a population-total expansion divided by known N and an element SRS mean. Sample sizes match expected SSU count.

load_bearing.statement: A finite population is partitioned into M ≥ 1 nonempty PSUs U_i, with fixed values y_ij, totals T_i = Σ_j y_ij and T = Σ_i T_i. One-stage cluster sampling selects PSUs and observes all their SSUs; SRSWOR assigns equal probability to every m-element PSU subset, 1 ≤ m ≤ M.

The joint sampling mass is p_1(S_1) times the product of p_2i(S_i) over selected PSUs. With all first-order inclusion probabilities positive, T̂_i = Σ_{j∈S_i} y_ij/π_(j|i)^(2) and T̂ = Σ_{i∈S_1} T̂_i/π_i^(1).
For M ≥ 2 fixed PSU totals and uniform SRSWOR of 1 ≤ m ≤ M PSUs, T̂_C = (M/m)Σ_{i∈S_1}T_i satisfies E_d[T̂_C] = T and Var_d(T̂_C) = M²(1−m/M)S_T²/m.
